text:
maria: Quick sync — proposal to align enforcement windows for per-org and per-key quotas. Right now we double-count bursts (org sliding window + key fixed window) which confuses users and leads to surprising throttles. Sketch below, please react with :thumbsup: if you agree or leave comments.

aj: tl;dr current state: per-org = sliding 60s leaky bucket; per-key = 1m fixed token-bucket. If a client sends a short burst across two keys they can often sneak past one limit then get clobbered by the other.

kyle: Proposal: unify to a shared token-bucket model with two dimensions: request_rate and token_rate. Each org has a shared pool; keys draw from org pool but also have small per-key sub-buckets. Burst is handled by a short-term "burst budget" that refills slowly. Benefits: single source of truth for remaining capacity, easier console display, simpler telemetry.

samantha: UX/telemetry notes: console should show both org remaining + key remaining, and a timeline of recent throttles with reason code (throttled_org | throttled_key | throttled_tokens). Can we add the next-refill ETA and a short explanation tooltip? e.g., "Burst budget will refill 25% every 5m" 

dmitri: compatibility: need migration path. Rolling change behind feature-flag and staged on opt-in orgs for 2 weeks. Fallback: if new model results in less capacity for an org, we should auto-apply a temporary grace window (1h) and generate a billing-safe alert to account team. Suggested rollout steps below.

maria: Config sketch (not final):
```json
{
  "enforcement": {
    "window_seconds": 60,
    "org_capacity": 1200,
    "per_key_capacity": 300,
    "burst_budget": {
      "capacity": 900,
      "refill_seconds": 300
    },
    "dimensions": ["request_rate","token_rate"]
  }
}
```
This uses a 60s base window, an org shared pool (org_capacity), small per-key sub-pools, and a burst_budget that can be spent before drawing down the org pool.

aj: edge case: embeddings + batching. A single request can consume many tokens but few call counts. We should enforce both dimensions independently and return clear error codes: 429:throttle_req, 429:throttle_tokens, 429:throttle_burst. Console should map those to human text.

kyle: agreed. Enforce the higher of the two checks (if either denies, reject). Also add a cheap pre-check in the SDK server-side proxy so we can early-reject obviously-excessive token requests and avoid spending expensive compute.

samantha: telemetry implementation: add counters to middleware: org_tokens_used, key_tokens_used, burst_spent, throttle_reason. Instrument with a sample span that includes reason and remaining_budget. Dashboards: top throttled orgs (24h), throttle rate per model, and latency impact during throttle events.

dmitri: rollout plan (short):
- feature-flag rollout to 5 pilot orgs (opt-in)
- compare throttle rates, support tickets, and cost delta for 72h
- expand to 20% of traffic for 7 days, adjust parameters
- global flip with 30d soft-grace where we auto-raise org_capacity by 10% if we detect regressions
Include an API migration endpoint to preview effective quotas for a given org+key.

maria: console UX: add per-route breakdown, color-coded remaining (green/yellow/red), and a hover panel showing last 100 throttle events and links to support ticket template. Also add an explanation wizard for plan mapping: Free/pro/enterprise -> base capacities + burst allowances.

aj: question: pricing mapping. Free should keep very small burst (one-time credits) and low sustained token_rate. Pro gets modest burst and higher token rate. Enterprise has negotiable capacity and can buy reserved burst (like credits). We need to feed this into billing so usage overage alerts can fire before throttles.

kyle: agree on billing hooks. Add a soft-throttle stage at 80% of quota that toggles a warning header and increments warning_issued telemetry. This gives customers time to upgrade before hard-throttle.

samantha: will add dashboard mockups to the design board. For telemetry, we need stable reason codes and sample spans by next week so QE can write deterministic tests.

maria: thanks — can everyone add a :thumbsup: if you're OK with the approach or comment with objections. I'll book 30m follow-up Wed.

deploy-bot: scheduled deploy-window notice: feature-flag service will be available for rollout starting 03:00 UTC tomorrow.

maria: noted, thanks.
